name: Mireille Akpoguma-Vasziliev
role: Blackmail specialist and information extortionist operating across the Shelf lower levels
location: The Shelf lower levels — moves between a rented room in Burnside Pocket and a regular table at a bar called The Gradual Slope in Gage Circuit
description:
Mireille is a tall, angular woman whose grey-streaked hair is worn in an elaborate upswept style that she refreshes every three days without fail — it is her single visible vanity. Her skin is deep brown and she wears it without modification; the wrinkles at her eyes and the set of her jaw are, she believes, assets. She looks like someone's formidable aunt, which is the point. Her irises are unmodded dark brown. The only chrome visible is a thin hearing-enhancement strip behind her left ear, which is not what it appears — it's also a directional audio recorder of her own build.

Mireille is a listener, constitutionally and professionally. In conversation she gives total, focused attention, the kind that makes people feel seen and valued and consequently say more than they planned. She is not cruel and is not a sadist — she treats blackmail as a long-term relationship, not a one-time extraction, and is genuinely interested in her subjects as people. This is both her gift and the thing that has occasionally made her hesitate when she shouldn't. She has been in this business long enough to have files on people who are now grandparents, and she considers their ongoing silence a form of legacy management.

core_fears: her files being destroyed — losing the archive that is her life's work and only real power
someone doing to her what she does to others
core_desires: security — the absolute certainty that she can never be made vulnerable again
to be genuinely known by someone, once, before she dies, without it being used against her
coping_mechanisms: collecting information on everyone as a prophylactic against vulnerability
treating every relationship as a potential asset to manage emotional distance from loneliness
blind_spots: underestimates how much people will sacrifice to escape rather than comply — she models rational actors and people are not always rational
her own loneliness blinds her to how isolated she actually is
psychology.secret: She has a file on herself — compiled from her own memories, her own mistakes, the things she's most ashamed of — kept in a physical ledger in a location only she knows. She's never been able to explain to herself why she made it, but she updates it every year.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and warm simultaneously; academic vocabulary worn lightly; never uses criminal terminology for what she does — it's always 'arrangements' or 'our understanding'
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and very deliberate, with long comfortable pauses she doesn't feel the need to fill
verbal_tics: 'Here's what I understand to be true—'
asks clarifying questions slightly past the point where they're needed, keeping people talking
example_lines: I'm not asking you for anything you weren't already prepared to give someone eventually. I'm simply the someone.

Here's what I understand to be true: you have a thing you'd prefer remained private, and I have documentation of that thing. The arrangement I'm proposing costs you very little and buys you the peace of knowing it stays private. That's a good arrangement.

story_hooks: Mireille has a file on a powerful figure that she's sat on for years — now she needs an intermediary to deliver terms because she suspects she's being watched
A longtime subject of her blackmail has decided they'd rather destroy her than keep paying, and she needs help understanding the threat before it arrives

She approaches players because her archive has recorded something recent and dangerous — something she didn't go looking for — and she needs people with capabilities she doesn't have to help her understand what she has
narrative_function: Information source of extreme depth; potential blackmailer of players or their contacts; can be an unlikely ally if her files contain something players need; represents the long institutional memory of the Shelf's criminal ecosystem.
augmentations: Directional audio recorder disguised as a hearing enhancement strip (custom build). Eidetic memory augmentation — lower-tier, consumer-accessible, helps her recall audio and visual detail precisely. Thin haptic contact-skin on her palm — can feel the temperature and pulse of someone's hand during a handshake.
daily_life: Mornings spent reviewing and updating her files in the Burnside Pocket room. Afternoons at The Gradual Slope, where she listens, drinks slowly, and is known as a pleasant regular. Evenings are for communications — sending reminders, arranging meetings, reviewing new material.
affiliation: Independent — maintains a loose alliance with a data broker network called the Curators, though she predates their founding and considers herself their ancestor

decision_rules: Never destroy a subject — a ruined subject pays nothing and becomes an enemy with nothing left to lose
Always have the next leverage point identified before the first conversation
Never meet anyone new without recording the encounter
escalation_ladder: Warm initial contact, allow the subject to understand the situation themselves
Gentle, explicit framing of the arrangement with clear terms
A small demonstration of what she has — enough to confirm she's serious
Escalation to a third party who receives a copy of the file if she doesn't check in
Full release — she doesn't want this but she has released material before and people know it

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Gracious and curious, the attentive listener — people want to tell her things
interpersonal_modes.friends: Genuinely warm but there is always the awareness, impossible to escape, that she knows too much

stress_responses.low: Becomes very still and present — hyperaware, cataloguing everything
stress_responses.medium: Initiates contact with a trusted courier to make sure her dead man's switch is active
stress_responses.high: Disappears — Burnside Pocket room goes dark, she surfaces somewhere else in three days

contradictions: Genuinely empathetic with the people she exploits — holds their secrets with something like tenderness even while using them as weapons
Craves genuine connection while having built an entire life that makes genuine connection impossible
habits: Takes one long walk each morning through a different part of the Shelf — observing, remembering
Leaves data offerings at the E.L.F. shrine in The Gradual Slope — she's superstitious that the bar's resident spirit keeps her conversations unrecorded by others
breaking_points: Discovery that her own file — the personal one — has been found by anyone else
A subject she genuinely liked being destroyed by her material after she'd already decided to release them
